activities.name: ggConstitMatch

config.prompt: The groupings are real — pair each diagnostic with what it shows:

pairs.right: the string behaves as one unit: a constituent
the group survives on its own

pairs.left: recursion — 'the rat the cat the dog chased killed ate the malt'
pairs.right: a finite rule set producing infinite sentences

config.why: Phrase structure rules generate the groupings and recursion makes the system unbounded — Syntactic Structures' (1957) central demonstration.

activities.caption: drag the divider — one skeleton, two mirrorings
activities.name: ggHeadCompare

config.prompt: X-bar gives every phrase the same architecture — drag the divider:

before.label: English — heads first
before.text: The verb precedes its object: eat apples. 'Eats apples', 'fond of apples' and 'in the garden' are structurally parallel.

after.label: Japanese — heads last
after.text: ringo-o taberu — 'apple-eat'. The same skeleton, mirrored: a parametric setting, not a structural difference.

config.why: One architecture for noun, verb, adjective and preposition phrases — the 1970s generalisation, and the source of typology.

config.prompt: One setting, many consequences — file each observation:
buckets: pro-drop ON — the subject may be silent
pro-drop OFF — an overt subject is demanded
evidence the options were available all along

items.label: hablo — 'I speak' with no pronoun at all
*'speak' as a full English clause — impossible
rich verb agreement arrives with the setting
free subject positioning arrives with the setting
a bilingual French–Italian child keeps the two settings distinct from the earliest multiword speech

config.why: Languages vary in correlated bundles, as if switches rather than dials — and children set parameters fast and rarely revisit.

activities.anchor: passive derives one structure from another
activities.caption: find the line the movement rules forbid
activities.name: ggIslandsSpot

config.prompt: One line of this derivation summary breaks the constraints — click it:
lines: Deep structure: every phrase sits in its base-generated position.
wh-movement displaces a questioned phrase: 'What did she see?' — leaving a trace.
do-support inserts the otherwise illegal auxiliary: 'Does she like it?'
A question may lift any phrase out of a relative clause — movement is unconstrained.
Crain and Nakayama (1987): children front the main-clause auxiliary without the linear-rule error.
config.correction: Islands block extraction: 'What did she see the report that criticised?' is impossible.
config.why: The constraints' specificity is the argument's workhorse: children never hear enough data to learn which infinite set of sentences is impossible, yet every speaker knows.

activities.anchor: Chomsky's hierarchy of automata measures the theory exactly
activities.caption: rank the machines by the strength language needs
activities.name: ggHierarchyOrder

config.prompt: From weakest to strongest — order the machines natural language pushes through:
items: Finite-state machines: provably cannot handle English's centre-embedding
Context-free grammars: handle much of it
Mildly context-sensitive: Swiss German's cross-serial dependencies (Shieber, 1985) force the step up
config.why: Each step up the strength ladder buys exactly the embedding natural language demands — the precision parsing algorithms implement.

activities.anchor: so word order can go free
activities.caption: true or false — case doing syntax's work
activities.name: ggCaseJudge

statements.s: In German 'Den Mann beißt der Hund', the accusative den tells you the man is the one being bitten whatever the position.
statements.why: Rich case stamps each noun phrase with its structural role — nominative subject, accusative object, dative recipient.

statements.s: English lost most case marking, and the pronouns resist the loss.
statements.why: *'him saw she' fails precisely because pronouns still compute case.

statements.s: The who/whom distinction is collapsing exactly where case no longer computes.
statements.why: The residue shows where syntax still demands the marking.

statements.s: Position is the deep structure; case merely decorates it.
statements.why: Case-rich languages prove the grammatical roles are real independently of position.

activities.caption: fill the two halves of Frege's split
activities.name: ggFregeCloze

config.text: Frege's 1892 distinction: %%0%% is the thing itself; %%1%% is the mode of presentation — which is why 'the morning star' and 'the evening star' share one and not the other.
config.hint: One is what the expression points at; the other is how it presents it.
config.why: Semantics' generative engine is compositionality — compute the whole from the parts — and Montague's lambda calculus turns that into truth conditions.

activities.anchor: it turns out all of them passed
activities.caption: asserted or merely implied? walk the distinction
activities.name: ggImplicatureBranch

config.root: Grice's maxims at work — one report, one inference, one courtroom distinction.

start.text: You told the examiner: 'Some students passed.' In fact every single one did. What did you assert?

choices.label: 'Not all passed' — as part of what I said
choices.feedback: Entailments cannot be cancelled without contradiction. Try cancelling this one.

choices.label: Only 'some passed' — the rest rides as an inference
choices.feedback: Test by cancellation: 'Some — indeed all — of the students passed' stands without contradiction.

entail.text: The cancellation succeeds, so 'not all' was never entailed. It was an implicature — generated by the maxim 'be informative', cancelable, not asserted.

choices.label: So where does the distinction earn its keep?

cancel.text: The inference 'not all' came from Grice's maxim of informativeness — implied, not stated.

choices.label: Where does the distinction do real work?

legal.text: Misleading by implicature versus lying by entailment — real legal and ethical work, made principled by the framework rather than intuition alone. Austin's speech acts extend it: utterances do things — promising, naming — beyond stating.

config.why: Implicatures differ from entailments precisely in being cancelable — the inference is real, but it was never part of what was said.
